title: Kesariwada Ganpati
text:
Kesariwada Ganpati (केसरीवाडा गणपती) — 5 (Panchva Manacha), located in Narayan Peth, Pune, established 1893 (1894 per some sources).

History: Kesariwada Ganpati is the Ganpati Lokmanya Tilak himself installed in 1893 inside Kesariwada, his personal residence — the very place from which he launched Sarvajanik Ganeshotsav, turning a household ritual into a mass movement against British rule. The Kesari newspaper, Tilak's Marathi journal for the freedom movement, was also published from here. A Tilak museum inside the Wada displays the historic palanquin used in the mandal's procession, and a statue of Tilak stands behind the Ganpati idol.

Idol/Deity: Idol housed within the historic Kesariwada; a Tilak statue stands behind it; simple murti, profound historical weight.

Temple/Mandir address: Kesariwada, 619, RB Kumthekar Road, Narayan Peth, Pune 411030. Festival pandal address: TO UPDATE — confirm 2026 pandal address via mandal. Maps link: TO UPDATE — check Kesari Trust social media in August 2026. Coordinates: 18.5135, 73.853.

Aarti timings — Morning: 6:00 AM; Evening: 7:00 PM.

Special events during the 10 days: Tilak Museum open to visitors; freedom movement heritage walk; traditional procession with historic palanquin.
